summary: A Hopf-Rinow Part II design, reusing existing connection, metric, curvature and volume owners. Eighteen nodes give actual-function Jacobi/index/Riccati calculus in a fixed parallel model. The intrinsic frame bridge, global comparisons and variational topology remain explicit source and implementation obligations. No stage is closed.

nodes.title: Wronskian of two fields
nodes.statement: For actual curves J,L define W(t)=<J'(t),L(t)>-<J(t),L'(t)> on the fixed real inner-product space.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space. The definition uses total derivatives; analytic uses carry explicit regularity hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the actual derivative and existing real inner product. No Jacobi equation or constancy is built into this definition.
Its swap and diagonal identities follow from real inner-product symmetry.

sources.locator: Section 2 Jacobi equation, p.3; the Wronskian conservation law is derived here
sources.match: Explicit fixed-frame refinement. The intrinsic frame and variation bridges are separate RG.1 targets, not assumptions in a new object.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the Wronskian
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space and J,L are actual functions.
proofSteps: Unfold the actual function.

sources.locator: Section 2 Jacobi equation, p.3; evaluation of the defined paired-field expression
sources.match: An explicit fixed-frame definition and calculation, not a claim of a separately printed source lemma.

nodes.title: Derivative of the Wronskian
nodes.statement: For C2 J,L at t, W'(t)=<J''(t),L(t)>-<J(t),L''(t)>.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space; both curves are C2 on a neighbourhood of t.
proofSteps: Apply the inner-product derivative twice. The two terms <J',L'> cancel. C2 regularity supplies differentiability of the derivative curves.
acceptance: Actual second derivatives are required; a formal jet is not substituted.

sources.locator: Section 2 Jacobi equation and the integration-by-parts calculation of Proposition 3.7, p.7
sources.match: The paired-field derivative calculation is supplied here from the actual inner-product derivative rule.

nodes.title: Wronskian conservation
nodes.statement: If J and L solve J''+KJ=0 and L''+KL=0 on [a,b] for the same pointwise symmetric K, then W(J,L) is constant there.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, and J,L are C2 at each point of [a,b]. K is a function into continuous linear endomorphisms, symmetric at every point of this interval. Both displayed ODEs hold there.
proofSteps: Substitute both equations into the derivative identity. Symmetry of K makes the two remaining terms cancel.
The Wronskian is differentiable; its zero derivative is integrable. Apply the pinned FTC on [a,t] to each t in [a,b]. No ODE existence theorem is presumed.
acceptance: Different coefficients or a nonsymmetric coefficient do not give this conservation law.

sources.locator: Section 2 Jacobi equation, p.3; paired-solution conservation deduced from that equation
sources.match: Explicit fixed-frame deduction; the intrinsic frame and variation bridges remain RG.1 targets.

nodes.title: Index form in a parallel model
nodes.statement: Define I_K(V,W)=integral_a^b (<V',W'>-<KV,W>) using the existing oriented Lebesgue interval integral. There is no factor one-half.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space; K is an actual function into continuous linear endomorphisms and V,W are actual fields. Analytic uses carry regularity and integrability; positivity requires ordered endpoints.
proofSteps: Use actual derivatives, a continuous-linear-operator-valued coefficient and the existing integral. The displayed expression is the fixed-frame form, not a manifold Hessian by definition.

Its geometric relation to half-energy is proved only after the intrinsic second-variation and parallel-frame bridge. Regularity/integrability precede analytic uses; divergent total integrals carry no geometric meaning.
acceptance: Reversing endpoints changes the sign. A constant field can have negative index for a positive potential.

sources.match: Explicit fixed-frame refinement. The intrinsic parallel-frame and variation bridges are separate RG.1 targets.

nodes.title: Integrability of the index density
nodes.statement: Continuous K and C1 fields on neighbourhoods of all points of [a,b] give an interval-integrable index density.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], and V,W are C1 at each point of that interval.
proofSteps: C1 gives continuous fields and continuous actual derivatives on the closed interval. Continuous operator evaluation and inner product make the density continuous.
Apply compact-interval continuous integrability. This establishes the hypotheses used by subsequent integral arithmetic.
acceptance: No smoothness of K beyond continuity is needed.

sources.match: Integrability of the actual density is proved explicitly using the pinned analytic theorem.

nodes.title: Additivity in the first field
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], and U,V,W are C1 at every point of that interval.
proofSteps: Differentiate the sum and expand the continuous linear operator and inner product.
Use index-integrability for both densities and integral_sub applied to the negative second summand, equivalently integral addition.
acceptance: Linearity of total differentiation is not asserted for arbitrary nonsmooth fields.

sources.match: The bilinear law is expanded with the required integrability hypotheses.

nodes.title: Scaling in the first field
nodes.statement: Under the stated regularity, I_K(c V,W)=c I_K(V,W) for constant real c.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], and V,W are C1 at every point of that interval.
proofSteps: Differentiate constant scalar multiplication and expand both bilinear terms. Factor the scalar through the interval integral.

sources.match: The real scaling identity uses the existing interval integral.

nodes.title: Symmetry of the index form
nodes.statement: If K(t) is symmetric on [a,b], then I_K(V,W)=I_K(W,V).
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, and <K(t)u,v>=<u,K(t)v> for all t in [a,b] and u,v in E. Equality of densities needs no further differentiability premise.
proofSteps: Use symmetry of the real inner product and <KV,W>=<V,KW> pointwise. The equal densities have equal integrals.
acceptance: Symmetry is a hypothesis on the actual K, not part of the definition.

sources.match: The fixed-frame coefficient symmetry gives the displayed density equality.

nodes.title: Green identity with endpoints
nodes.statement: For C2 V, C1 W and continuous K, I_K(V,W)=[<V',W>]_a^b-integral_a^b <V''+KV,W>.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], V is C2 and W is C1 at every point of that interval.
proofSteps: Differentiate <V',W> using the existing inner-product rule. Rearrangement of its two terms gives the identity of densities.
All densities are continuous and integrable. Apply FTC to <V',W>, then integral subtraction. K need not be symmetric.
acceptance: The endpoint pairings are retained unless their actual values vanish.

sources.match: The fixed-frame integration-by-parts formula with all endpoint terms retained.

nodes.title: Green identity across a corner
nodes.statement: For two separately C2 pieces U on [a,c] and V on [c,b], continuous at c, and a C1 test field W, the sum of their index forms is the outer boundary term minus <V'(c)-U'(c),W(c)> minus the two residual integrals.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=c<=b, and K is continuous on [a,b]. U is C2 at each point of [a,c], V is C2 at each point of [c,b], W is C1 at each point of [a,b], and U(c)=V(c).
proofSteps: Apply the preceding Green identity separately on the two intervals.

Collect the two evaluations at c. They are <U'(c),W(c)>-<V'(c),W(c)>, the negative right-minus-left derivative jump. Continuity makes this a genuine broken-field statement, although the algebraic identity itself needs only the common test value.
acceptance: The tent field t on [0,1] and 2-t on [1,2] has jump -2. Omitting it gives a false identity against the constant test field.

sources.match: The explicit two-piece specialization retains the source jump sign; finite-partition gluing remains an intrinsic-stage obligation.

nodes.title: Jacobi fields reduce the index to the boundary
nodes.statement: If J''+KJ=0, then I_K(J,W)=[<J',W>]_a^b. In particular, a test field zero at both endpoints is annihilated.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], J is C2 and W is C1 at every point of that interval, and the displayed ODE holds there.
proofSteps: Substitute the actual Jacobi equation into Green's residual integral. The integrand is zero; the endpoints remain.
acceptance: A Jacobi equation alone does not make the index zero for nonzero endpoint data.

sources.match: The forward boundary-vanishing consequence is proved explicitly; the full annihilator characterization remains separate.

nodes.title: Derivative-energy bound for a nonpositive coefficient
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], V is C1 at each point of that interval, and the quadratic coefficient inequality holds for every v.
proofSteps: Use <V',V'>=||V'||^2. The potential term enters with a minus sign and is nonnegative after negation.
Both densities are continuous. Apply interval-integral monotonicity and nonnegativity with a<=b.
acceptance: This is a derivative-energy bound, not a lower bound by the position norm without a boundary/Poincare condition.

sources.match: Explicit nonpositive-coefficient consequence of the displayed fixed-frame integral.

nodes.title: Zero index detects the zero anchored field
nodes.statement: For a<b, continuous nonpositive K and a C1 field V with V(a)=0, equality I_K(V,V)=0 forces V(t)=0 for every t in [a,b].
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, V is C1 at every point of [a,b], and <K(t)v,v><=0 there for every v. The strict interval inequality and the anchoring condition are retained.
proofSteps: The preceding bound and nonnegativity force the integral of ||V'||^2 to be zero.
If the continuous squared derivative were positive anywhere on [a,b], the pinned strict-positivity theorem would make its integral positive. Thus V'=0 at every point.
Use vector-valued FTC on [a,t] and V(a)=0. No a.e.-to-pointwise statement is assumed without the continuity step.
acceptance: Without anchoring, a nonzero constant field for K=0 is a counterexample. The condition a<b excludes a collapsed interval.

sources.locator: Equation (5) and Proposition 3.7, printed p.7; zero-energy consequence derived here
sources.match: The fixed-model detection proof supplies its pointwise continuity step, not merely an almost-everywhere inference.

nodes.title: Two-zero uniqueness for nonpositive coefficients
nodes.statement: A C2 solution of J''+KJ=0 for continuous nonpositive K that vanishes at both ends of a nondegenerate interval vanishes throughout that interval.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<b, J is C2 at every point of [a,b], K is continuous there, and <K(t)v,v><=0 for every v. The ODE and J(a)=J(b)=0 hold.
proofSteps: Apply the Jacobi boundary formula with W=J; its endpoints make the index zero.
Apply the anchored zero-detection theorem. This proves the fixed-frame assertion without importing intrinsic conjugate-point theory.
acceptance: For K=1, sin(t) on [0,pi] is a nonzero two-zero solution; the coefficient sign cannot be dropped.

sources.locator: Equation (5) and the Jacobi boundary consequence of Proposition 3.7
sources.match: Explicit fixed-frame deduction; the intrinsic absence-of-conjugate-points conclusion needs the RG.1 comparison.

nodes.title: Riccati square-completion identity
nodes.statement: If the actual C1 symmetric operator field S satisfies S'+S composed with S+K=0 at t, the index density equals <V'-SV,W'-SW> plus the derivative of <SV,W>.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space; S,V,W are C1 at t; S(t) is symmetric; the displayed operator identity holds at t. K is an actual operator-valued function.
proofSteps: Differentiate the actual operator evaluation S(t)V(t) by the bounded bilinear rule and then its pairing with W.
Expand <V'-SV,W'-SW>. Symmetry cancels the cross terms, and <SV,SW>=<S squared V,W>. The remaining S'+S squared term is -K by the equation.
acceptance: An algebraic square without the derivative of S is wrong when S varies.

sources.locator: Equation (26) and Lemma 3.3, printed p.6; the square-completion is proved here
sources.match: A deduction from the actual Riccati equation, not an assumed factorization or a claim of global solvability.

nodes.title: Integrated Riccati factorization
nodes.statement: On [a,b], I_K(V,W)=integral <V'-SV,W'-SW>+[<SV,W>]_a^b when the actual C1 symmetric S solves the Riccati equation throughout and K is continuous.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous on [a,b], S,V,W are C1 at every point of that interval, S(t) is symmetric and S'+S squared+K=0 holds throughout.
proofSteps: Integrate the preceding pointwise identity. C1 fields and S give continuous densities and derivative of the boundary pairing.
Apply FTC to that pairing and integral arithmetic. No claim that S exists past a singular time is included.
acceptance: For scalar K=1, S=cot(t) is available only away from its poles.

sources.locator: Equation (26) and Lemma 3.3, printed p.6; integral deduction
sources.match: The integral identity and its endpoints are proved from the explicit differential equation.

nodes.title: Dirichlet positivity from a Riccati solution
nodes.statement: With the preceding hypotheses and V(a)=V(b)=0, I_K(V,V)=integral ||V'-SV||^2 >= 0.
hypotheses: E is a real Hilbert space, a<=b, K is continuous, S and V are C1 at each point of [a,b], S is symmetric and satisfies S'+S squared+K=0 there, and V vanishes at both endpoints.
proofSteps: Use the factorization with W=V. The endpoints vanish by the actual endpoint values.
The remaining inner square is nonnegative and the interval is ordered. Apply the existing integral nonnegativity theorem.
acceptance: This does not construct S from a Jacobi tensor or establish absence of conjugate points without that separate argument.

sources.locator: Equation (26), p.6, combined with the index identity
sources.match: The nonnegative integral follows only on the stated regular Riccati interval.

Use normal neighbourhoods, Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and the already-owned first variation/half-energy. This Part II adds second variation, not a duplicate energy or geodesic definition.
Use the pointwise/global Hopf-Rinow equivalences and existence of minimizing geodesics under the stated connected smooth finite-dimensional completeness hypotheses.
Use the actual curvature tensor, sectional/Ricci conventions and Riemannian volume measure, not new competing carriers. Check sign and Ricci normalization against the +Jacobi/-index conventions.

Use the early geometric cut-locus/injectivity-radius and volume-nullity interface without importing transport plans or a downstream Bishop-Gromov theorem. Split a finer early supplier if necessary to avoid a stage cycle; generic conjugate-field computations are supplied here.

remaining: Elaborate the 18 fixed-frame nodes and tests at the pins. Prove every regularity and integrability obligation on the actual function carriers; the suggested file is uncompiled.
Complete the intrinsic parallel-frame, curvature and second-variation comparison and the arbitrary-piecewise field/partition API. The two-piece lemma is not its replacement.

Source-decompose the full Jacobi-tensor construction, index lemma and Rauch/Riccati/Hessian comparisons, with actual singular-endpoint limits and domains. Refine the cut-locus supplier to prevent cycles.

Turn the inspected Bonnet-Myers and Hadamard-Cartan arguments into exact manifold/covering declarations. Supply the lifted-metric and completeness comparisons, not merely topological existence of a cover.
Prove the point-polar integration bridge and determinant/trace estimates; complete the equality and rigidity arguments. Respect the corrections recorded for the source normalization.

Read and decompose the complete finite-dimensional approximation, minimax and Morse-index proofs, not just the inspected propositions and statements. Establish the free-loop endpoint and homotopy prerequisites.
